updates.name: Robyn Barbato
updates.bio: Senior research microbiologist at the U.S. Army ERDC Cold Regions Research and Engineering Laboratory (CRREL), where she heads the soil microbiology team. Her group cores roughly 40,000-year-old permafrost in the Permafrost Tunnel at Fox, Alaska, revives its microbes in Hanover, New Hampshire, and has reported 26 new species studied as leads for cold-regions biotechnology.
updates.research_interests: Permafrost microbiology; reviving and describing novel microbial species from ~40,000-year-old permafrost (CRREL Permafrost Tunnel, Fox, Alaska); mechanisms of microbial survival at sub-zero temperatures; cold-regions biotechnology (anti-icing coatings, frostbite protection)

Earlier he became full professor at the University of Texas Medical Branch's Marine Biomedical Institute. His lab studies rapid adaptive camouflage and body patterning, chiefly in cephalopods, linking field behavior, vision and skin neurobiology.

updates.name: Roger W. Ruess
updates.bio: Ecosystem ecologist; Professor Emeritus and Senior Research Associate at the University of Alaska Fairbanks Institute of Arctic Biology, on the biology faculty 1989-2020. His boreal forest work, much of it within the Bonanza Creek LTER program he led, covers soil organic nitrogen, fine-root dynamics, herbivore effects on succession, alder-Frankia symbioses and drought-linked aspen mortality.
updates.research_interests: Boreal forest ecosystem ecology; organic nitrogen cycling in soils; belowground carbon partitioning and fine-root turnover; vertebrate herbivores in succession and state transitions; genomic study of soil bacterial and fungal communities; alder-Frankia-mycorrhizal interactions; carbon and drought stress in fungal-pathogen-driven aspen mortality in interior Alaska

updates.name: Roni Avissar
updates.bio: Atmospheric scientist and Rosenstiel School Professor at the University of Miami; he led the school as dean from 2009 to 2025. He builds numerical and analytical models of ocean-land-atmosphere interaction, developed a helicopter-based observing platform, and has studied how Amazon deforestation alters rainfall. Earlier he chaired civil and environmental engineering at Duke University.
updates.research_interests: Numerical and analytical modeling of ocean-land-atmosphere interactions across scales; helicopter-based atmospheric observation; effects of Amazon basin deforestation on regional and global precipitation; improving weather (including hurricane) forecasting and climate models
